text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami denies speculation that he is to step down from leadership of the Nationalist Party, defeated by the Labour Party in the general election last October.
- Malta and Egypt sign tourism accord during visit to Cairo by Maltese Foreign Minister George Vella.
- To make adoption of children from Brazil easier, Maltese government is making arrangements with an Italian organisation which helps childless couples adopt such children.
- Prime Minister Alfred Sant reacts to opposition claims of political transfers in the civil service, issues documents to prove political transfers under the former government.
- Some 80 percent of computer programmes in Malta are copied, according to estimate by representatives of computer companies.

- Opposition leader Fenech Adami says some decisions by new Labour government have started to harm Malta's image abroad, and argues Malta should continue its efforts to join the European Union. The EU application was frozen by the present government.
